canonical_name: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol — RFC 5321 living transport lineage

last_known_use.notes: SMTP remains the basic Internet mail-transfer protocol family.

addressing: Uses mail envelope sender/recipient addresses and DNS-assisted routing rather than defining the message-format address grammar alone.
routing_or_forwarding: Mail relay and routing behavior cooperates with DNS MX and local MTA policy.
error_control: Command/reply transaction semantics; delivery/retry/queue behavior is partly implementation/operational policy.
flow_or_congestion_control: Relies on underlying transport and application-level transaction/queue behavior rather than an SMTP-specific congestion-control algorithm.

survival.provenance_notes: Protocol lineage descends from RFC 821 and ESMTP extension work while retaining recognizable textual command/reply behavior.

open_questions: Trace ESMTP extension framework and important extensions.
Map sendmail/Postfix/Exim/qmail implementation behavior to standards revisions.
Separate mail transport from submission, message format and mailbox access.

related_artifacts.relation: transports messages represented by Internet Message Format
uses DNS mail-routing data such as MX in deployment

notes: SMTP is transport, not the complete email format/access system.
